title: 2026 TCS New York City Marathon — event entry page (methods, fees, drawing pools, key dates)
claims: The 2026 event is listed for Sunday, November 1, 2026 at 8:00 AM in New York City, Distance: Marathon; entry fees run from $0.00 to $333.11, and registration is closed.

Non-guaranteed general entry applications opened February 4 at 12:00 p.m. ET and closed February 25 at 11:59 p.m. ET; the drawing took place March 4; the Non-NYRR time qualifier application closed February 11 at 11:59 p.m. ET.

The non-guaranteed drawing runs three separate pools: NYC metro area (residents within 60 miles of New York City), National (U.S. residents outside the metro area, including Puerto Rico and other U.S. territories), and International (non-U.S. residents).

Guaranteed entry methods listed on the page: official charity partner, Official International Tour Operator, 9+1 program, 2025 virtual race completion, Team for Kids, Team for Climate, completed 15-plus marathons, NYRR Time Qualifiers, Non-NYRR Time Qualifiers, 5K/10K membership, 2025 cancellation, and the NYRR Race Free program.
Members who apply to the non-guaranteed general drawing are automatically entered into the NYRR Member-Only Second-Chance Drawing.

Once a guaranteed entry is claimed or a drawing applicant is accepted, all entry fees are non-refundable; fees may not be deferred or transferred; an accepted 2026 entrant may cancel and earn a non-complimentary guaranteed entry to 2027 but must claim it and pay the 2027 fees, and a runner who deferred in 2025 cannot defer a second time.

A newly registering runner without an NYRR best pace who expects to run 4:00:00 or faster may submit a placement time from a certified in-person marathon or half marathon completed between January 1, 2024 and September 7, 2026, by September 8, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET, for wave and corral placement.

The rules do not permit entry by a person intending to be pushed in a wheelchair, stroller or other equipment by another person; athletes with disabilities using wheelchair or allowable equipment must push themselves through the course, and official support runners may accompany but cannot push.
